Commentary.Commentary: We're back in action! Zimbabwe's openers, Brian Bennett and Ben Curran, are out in the middle to start the second innings. Meanwhile, the Kiwis are dealing with a setback as Nathan Smith's abdominal tear rules him out of bowling, leaving them a bowler short. Matt Henry will lead the charge, opening the attack for New Zealand.
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Zimbabwe put in a much-improved bowling performance on Day 2, which has kept them alive in this contest. Blessing Muzarabani rose to the occasion with three crucial wickets, while Tanaka Chivanga provided solid support with a couple of strikes. The spin trio maintained pressure throughout, chipping in with a wicket each, before Newman Nyamhuri finished things off. Now it’s over to the batters to deliver a strong response and make a game of it, while New Zealand will be aiming to restrict them to the lowest total possible.

A strong batting effort from New Zealand has given them a first-innings lead of 158 runs. While they might have hoped for an even bigger advantage after their solid start, credit goes to the hosts for bowling with discipline. The opening stand of 92 was the highest partnership for the Kiwis, and contributions kept coming throughout the order. Devon Conway led the way with a classy 88, while Daryl Mitchell’s composed 80, along with a key contribution from Nathan Smith, ensured they reached this commanding position.

Despite the setbacks, Daryl Mitchell has held firm at one end, steadily adding to the lead and remaining unbeaten on 48. He received solid support first from Mitchell Santner and now from Nathan Smith. New Zealand will be hoping he can continue to anchor the innings and, with help from the lower order, push the lead beyond 150 and possibly close in on 200. If they manage that, they’ll be well on their way to sealing control of this Test. Zimbabwe, however, will look to prevent that with the second new ball due shortly. They’ll be eager to wrap up the innings quickly and get back to batting. Join us at 1 pm GMT for all the action in the final session!

New Zealand would have aimed to tighten their grip on the game and push towards a commanding lead, but Zimbabwe’s disciplined bowling and smart plans ensured that didn’t happen. Tanaka Chivanga led the charge, striking early with the big scalp of Devon Conway, who fell just 12 short of a century. He added another soon after, while Blessing Muzarabani and Vincent Masekesa chipped in with one apiece, helping the hosts claim their first session of the Test.

SESSION SUMMARY - 80 runs and 4 wickets in 27 overs! Zimbabwe have shown plenty of grit in this session, proving they won’t back down easily. The hosts toiled hard with the ball and earned their rewards, snaring four vital wickets. They still trail in the contest by 105 runs, but their spirited effort has given them a faint glimmer of hope to challenge the Kiwis.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! A good hour for Zimbabwe as they have made further inroads into the Kiwi batting line up. The lead is not that big, and the hosts will be looking to break this partnership and then get through the tail quickly to stay in the game. The wicket has enough for both seamers and spinners, and batting is not that easy. New Zealand are still ahead in this game, and they know that if they manage to get a couple of big partnerships, they will have this game in the bag. Daryl Mitchell will be key for them in extending the lead above and beyond 100 runs. A very exciting phase of cricket awaits us. Also, Sikandar Raza to bowl after the break.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session! The players are making their way out to the middle with the sun shining brightly. Daryl Mitchell and Devon Conway will resume batting for New Zealand. Tanaka Chivanga will start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Zimbabwe's bowlers, particularly Blessing Muzarabani and Sikandar Raza, have bowled well, with Muzarabani taking two wickets and Raza claiming one. The Kiwis will look to extend their lead further in the post-Lunch session. We will be back at 10.40 am GMT.

Devon Conway and Henry Nicholls batted well, adding 66 runs for the second wicket. However, after Henry's dismissal, Rachin Ravindra walked out and didn't last long, failing to make a significant impact and giving an opening to the Zimbabwean bowling unit. Conway looks set for a century, and at the end of the session, he is on 87, while Daryl Mitchell is on 9.

The first session of Day 2 has wrapped up, with both teams having a fair share of success. Zimbabwe's early breakthrough, dismissing Will Young on the first ball, set the tone for a competitive session. New Zealand scored 82 runs while losing 3 wickets in 26 overs, setting the stage for an intriguing battle in the post-Lunch session.

Commentary.Commentary: We're all set for Day 2 of the Test match between Zimbabwe and New Zealand. The Kiwi openers, Will Young and Devon Conway, are ready to face the Zimbabwean bowlers. Blessing Muzarabani will kick-start the proceedings for the hosts. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Scott Styris is pitchside. He says that the pitch has a lot of grass, but there are a lot of indentations, and there is enough for the bowlers to trouble the batters. Adds that there will be variable bounce from the 6-8m area, and the batter needs to be patient. Ed Rainsford joins and says that there is some grouping on the wicket. Says Zimbabwe bowlers need to find consistency, and they will get the reward.

Matt Henry of New Zealand is up for a chat. Henry highlights the importance of patience and creating pressure over extended periods in Test cricket. He notes that the morning session showed movement, which helped the bowlers, but emphasizes the need to trust their lengths and believe that wickets will follow. Henry stresses the fine balance between finding the ideal length and avoiding leaking runs, praising his teammates for adapting well to the longer format after white-ball cricket. He believes in evolving one's game while maintaining continuity and consistency, which has been key to their success. Henry expects a crucial first session, with the new ball likely to swing and seam, and aims to get through the initial period without losing wickets, setting up New Zealand for the rest of the day. His focus on sustained pressure and challenging the batsmen suggests an intense battle ahead.

For Zimbabwe, taking wickets is crucial. The pitch has shown promise for both seamers and spinners. Blessing Muzarabani led pace attack and Sikandar Raza's spin department will need to lead from the front to make inroads into the Kiwi batting lineup. It's shaping up to be an exciting day of Test cricket, with the Kiwis chasing a hefty lead and the hosts trying to stage a comeback. Will the Kiwis dominate, or can Zimbabwe make a fight of it? We shall find out soon.

The visitors, New Zealand, have a brilliant opportunity to bat at length and impose a substantial lead on the hosts, Zimbabwe. Under Mitchell Santner's leadership, the Kiwis will aim to bat just once and then have a go at the Chevrons again. Devon Conway and Will Young will focus on seeing off the first hour without losing a wicket, and then look to accelerate towards big scores, with centuries within their reach.

Hello and welcome to everyone as we head into Day 2 of this Test match between Zimbabwe and New Zealand. Day 1 of the Test match saw New Zealand dominate Zimbabwe. The hosts were bowled out for 149, with Matt Henry taking 6/39 and Nathan Smith claiming 3/20. Zimbabwe's top order collapsed to 31/3, but Nick Welch and Craig Ervine showed resistance, adding 36 runs together. However, Henry's spell broke the partnership, and Zimbabwe's innings was eventually wrapped up. In response, New Zealand reached 92/0 at Stumps, with Devon Conway not out on 51 and Will Young not out on 41, batting comfortably, leaving them 57 runs behind with all 10 wickets in hand.

Right then, that is it from a slow Day 1 of this 1st Test, where New Zealand are in the driver's seat and will be eyeing a massive lead, while Zimbabwe will want to make early inroads on Day 2. The action resumes on 31st July, Thursday, at 8 am GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Matt Henry stole the spotlight with a sensational six-wicket haul, while Nathan Smith provided solid support with three scalps. The rest of the attack, especially the spinners, maintained relentless pressure, leaving Zimbabwe choked for runs and completely on the back foot. In response, Will Young and Devon Conway ensured New Zealand’s dominance carried into the final session, batting positively and scoring freely. Conway brought up a classy half-century as the visitors slashed the deficit to less than half. Zimbabwe shuffled their bowling options with pace and spin, but nothing broke through as they ended the day without a wicket.

After opting to bat first, Zimbabwe failed to justify their decision as they crumbled against a relentless Kiwi attack. Wickets fell at regular intervals with no substantial partnerships to steady the innings. While Nick Welch offered some resistance, it was the stand between Craig Ervine and Tafadzwa Tsiga that briefly raised hopes. However, the skipper’s unfortunate dismissal swung the momentum back to New Zealand, and the lower order offered little fight as Zimbabwe were bundled out for just 149.

It was a one-sided affair on the opening day as New Zealand dominated from start to finish, leaving Zimbabwe playing catch-up. A disciplined bowling display dismantled the hosts, and the Kiwi openers have capitalized brilliantly, reducing the deficit to just 57 runs and setting the platform for a massive first-innings lead.
